Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) Q4 2024 Earnings Conference Call July 30, 2024.

Executives Present:
Satya Nadella - Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
Amy Hood - Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
Brett Iversen - Vice President of Investor Relations

Analysts Present:
Keith Weiss - Morgan Stanley
Brent Thill - Jefferies
Mark Moerdler - Bernstein Research
Karl Keirstead - UBS

[SECTION: PREPARED_REMARKS]
Operator: Greetings, and welcome to the Microsoft Fiscal Year 2024 Fourth Quarter Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. A question-and-answer session will follow the formal presentation.

Brett Iversen: Good afternoon, and thank you for joining us today. On the call with me are Satya Nadella, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer; Amy Hood, Chief Financial Officer; and Alice Jolla, Chief Accounting Officer.

Satya Nadella: Thank you, Brett. We closed out our fiscal year with a strong quarter. Microsoft Cloud revenue surpassed $36.8 billion, up 21% year-over-year. As a company, we are committed to helping our customers apply our platforms and AI tools to drive business growth. Azure continued to take share. Our AI business alone exited the fiscal year at an annualized run rate of over $5 billion, driven by both training and inferencing workloads.

Amy Hood: Thank you, Satya. In Q4, total company revenue was $64.7 billion, up 15% year-over-year in constant currency. Gross margin percentage was 70%, relatively unchanged year-over-year. Operating income increased 15% to $27.9 billion.

Intelligent Cloud revenue was $28.5 billion, up 19% year-over-year. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 29% and 30% in constant currency, including 8 percentage points of growth from AI services. Demand for Azure AI services continues to be higher than our available capacity. We experienced some capacity constraints in external GPU clusters, which slightly moderated Azure growth in Q4.

Capital expenditures, including finance leases, were $19.0 billion in Q4, driven by investments to support cloud demand and accelerate our AI infrastructure footprint. Roughly half of our cloud and AI infrastructure spend was for long-lived assets that will support monetization over the next 15 years and beyond, including land and datacenter leases.

Guidance for Q1 Fiscal 2025: In Intelligent Cloud, we expect revenue of $28.6 billion to $28.9 billion, with Azure growth of 28% to 29% in constant currency. We expect Azure growth to accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2025 as our massive capital investments in datacenter capacity and AI chips come online.

[SECTION: ANALYST_QA]
Operator: Our first question comes from Keith Weiss with Morgan Stanley.
Keith Weiss: Thank you for taking the question. Amy, on Azure growth: 29% growth in Q4, guidance for 28% to 29% in Q1, with acceleration in the second half. Can you unpack the constraint? Is it purely GPU silicon allocation, or are power, data center shell, and networking also gating factors?

Amy Hood: Keith, thanks. The constraint in Q4 and heading into Q1 is primarily server availability and power infrastructure timing. Demand remains ahead of capacity. We saw strong demand across both frontier model training with OpenAI and enterprise inferencing. When new capacity is delivered, it is monetized immediately. As our supply comes online in the second half of fiscal 2025, we will be able to fulfill that backlog, which is why we expect Azure growth acceleration.
